stem: A drowsy child with suspected diabetic ketoacidosis is retching repeatedly; which bedside step is specifically mentioned to reduce immediate risk?

options.text: Lay the child flat to improve comfort
Nurse head up, monitor the airway, and consider an NGT if aspiration risk is present
Give oral rehydration solution before any monitoring
Remove all monitoring to reduce distress

explanation: Nurse head up, monitor the airway, and consider an NGT if aspiration risk is present. This is the bedside safety step specifically described to reduce aspiration risk in a drowsy child with suspected DKA who is retching.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the child should be positioned head up rather than lying flat when aspiration risk is a concern.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because oral carbohydrate is not the immediate safety step in a drowsy child with suspected DKA.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because head-up positioning, airway monitoring, and considering an NGT when aspiration risk is present are the specific bedside measures described to reduce immediate risk.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because oral rehydration is not the first safety measure for a drowsy child at risk of aspiration.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because ongoing monitoring is important in DKA and should not be removed to reduce distress.
